questions.prompt: A classifier has 8% overall error on a test set split into several subgroups. Which statement must be true?
options: Every subgroup has error close to 8%, because the average pulls all groups together.
At least one subgroup has error at or above 8% and at least one at or below 8%.
The largest subgroup has the error rate closest to 8%, because it dominates the average.
The smallest subgroup has the highest error rate, since small groups get less training data.
questions.explanation: The overall rate is a weighted average of the subgroup rates, so it lies between the smallest and largest subgroup rate. Nothing forces the groups to be equal or the smallest to be worst.

questions.prompt: A grasping log has two object types: 600 attempts with 18 failures, and 400 attempts with 22 failures. What is the overall failure rate, as a percentage with one decimal?
questions.explanation: (18+22)/(600+400) = 40/1000 = 4.0%. Pool counts; do not average 3% and 5.5% unweighted (that gives 4.25%).
questions.skillLabel: Pool counts into an overall rate

questions.prompt: True distances are y = [10, 12, 9] m and a sensor model predicts [11, 11, 11] m. What is the mean residual (observed minus predicted) in metres, to 2 decimals?
questions.explanation: Residuals are -1, +1, -2; their mean is -4/3 = -0.67 m, so the model over-predicts on average.

questions.prompt: A detector errs on 20% of dark images and 5% of bright images. Most dark images are also far from the camera. Within the far images the two lighting groups both err at 26%, and within near images both err at 2%. What is the best conclusion?
options: The test set is too small to conclude anything about either lighting or distance, so collect more first.
Darkness is the cause of the extra errors, so the team should add more night images to training.
Distance, not lighting, explains the gap in this data; the lighting gap is a composition effect.
The data prove that darkness has no effect on any detector, so lighting can be ignored from now on.
questions.explanation: Once distance is held fixed the lighting gap vanishes, so distance explains it here. That does not prove darkness never matters, only that this data does not support it.

questions.prompt: 3 failures occurred in 10 trials of a rare condition. What is the lower end of the 95% Wilson interval (z = 1.96) for the failure rate? Give a decimal to 3 places.
questions.skillLabel: Wilson interval for a small group

questions.prompt: You think a navigation stack fails more in corridors than in open rooms. Describe how you would test this explanation so that it could be rejected, including one confounder you would control.
rubric: States the explanation as a prediction with a baseline (overall or open-room failure rate) and a measurable metric.
Names a confounder (for example speed, map size, sensor type) and stratifies or matches on it.
States what result would reject the explanation and checks it on held-out or new runs, reporting group sizes.
questions.skillLabel: Design a test that can reject an explanation
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Which failure-taxonomy label is best for analysing a grasp detector?
options: Image looked dark and low-quality to the reviewer, so the model failed
The model was confused by the scene and made the wrong prediction here
Predicted box too small (class right, overlap with ground truth below threshold)
Needs more training data and a longer schedule to fix this kind of error
questions.explanation: A good label is observable from the case itself and points to a fix. The others are guesses about causes.

questions.prompt: Sketch (code or pseudocode) a function that, given a list of records with a 0/1 'error' field and a condition field, returns the error rate and count for every condition, and explain which edge case it must handle.
rubric: Accumulates count and error sum per group, then divides (no unweighted averaging of rates).
Returns n alongside the rate so small groups are visible.
Handles an empty or very small group (division by zero, minimum size, or interval).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
